title: A map of periodic complexes whose kernel and cokernel have finite length does not change the multiplicity
author: The Stacks Project Authors
work: Stacks Project, chapter chow.tex (Chow Homology and Chern Classes)
source_version: Stacks Project source tree, file chow.tex, corpus local snapshot 20261012
difficulty_reason: The lemma states that a map of $(2,1)$-periodic complexes whose kernel and cokernel have finite length preserves the multiplicity, provided the cohomology modules have finite length (statement lines 282-288). The proof splits the map through its kernel and cokernel using additivity of the multiplicity and then kills the two end terms through the vanishing criterion for finite length cohomology. The two-step reduction is the substance, so the claim is H2.
